top_story: U.S.-Iran tensions sharpened from March into 19 May, as Trump revived threats of a “big hit” after earlier coercive warnings against Iran’s power grid had already prompted Tehran to signal a wider regional response. That pressure now sits alongside a more immediate vulnerability in Gulf infrastructure after a drone strike near the UAE’s operating nuclear plant cut external power and forced a switch to backup generators, underscoring how regional conflict can spill into civilian systems with potentially transnational consequences. On Israel’s northern front, Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed at least 19 people on 19 May despite a ceasefire, and by 20 May Hezbollah’s expanding drone use was constraining much of Israel’s ground activity there. The combined picture is of a region where deterrence is eroding across multiple theaters, leaving civilian energy networks and border communities increasingly exposed to escalation.
